'''Myron Elmer "Max" Essex''' (born August 17, 1939) is the [[Mary Woodard Lasker]] Professor of Health Sciences, emeritus in the department of immunology and infectious diseases at [[Harvard University]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Myron Essex |url=https://www.hsph.harvard.edu/profile/myron-essex/ |website=Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health |date=5 January 2021 |publisher=The President and Fellows of Harvard College |access-date=29 July 2022}}</ref> chair of the [[Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health]] AIDS Initiative (HAI) in the department of immunology and infectious diseases,<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.aids.harvard.edu/ |title=Harvard School of Public Health AIDS Initiative |access-date=8 May 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190926183533/https://aids.harvard.edu/ |archive-date=26 September 2019 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and chair of the Botswana–Harvard AIDS Institute in [[Gaborone]], [[Botswana]]. Essex was one of the first to link animal and human [[retrovirus]]es to [[immunosuppressive]] disease, to suspect that a retrovirus was the cause of [[HIV/AIDS|AIDS]], and to determine that [[HIV]] could be transmitted through blood and blood products to [[hemophilia]]cs and recipients of blood transfusions. With collaborators, Essex also provided the first evidence that HIV could be transmitted by [[heterosexual]] intercourse.

In 1984, Essex identified [[gp120]], the virus surface protein that is used worldwide for blood screening, HIV detection, and epidemiological monitoring. With collaborators, including African microbiologist [[Souleymane Mboup]], he discovered the first [[simian immunodeficiency virus]], as well as [[HIV-2]].  Since 1986, he has developed programs for AIDS collaboration in [[Senegal]], [[Thailand]], [[Botswana]], [[India]], [[Mexico]], and [[China]]. In 1996, Essex helped establish the Botswana–Harvard Partnership for HIV Research and Education (now the Botswana–Harvard AIDS Institute). This is a collaboration between the Ministry of Health in Botswana and HAI.

==Biography==
Essex was born in [[Coventry, Rhode Island]] in 1939.<ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=92bJlWbPeKMC&q=%22Essex,+myron+elmer%22+1939 Who's Who in the World: 1991-1992]</ref> Essex earned his [[Doctor of veterinary medicine|D.V.M.]] from [[Michigan State University]] in 1967. He then earned his Ph.D. from [[University of California, Davis]], in 1970.

He has been married to Elizabeth Essex since 1967.  They have two daughters and five grandchildren.<ref name="haispotlight">[https://aids.harvard.edu/max-essex-the-persistent-investigator/ Henry MS.  Max Essex: The Persistent Investigator. March 11, 2016. HAI Blog. Spotlight, Winter 2016.]</ref>

Essex holds ten [[honorary doctorate]]s<ref name="haispotlight" /> and 15 patents and has received the [[Lasker Award]],<ref>[http://www.laskerfoundation.org/awards/1986clinical.htm 1986 Lasker Award] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100716162257/http://www.laskerfoundation.org/awards/1986clinical.htm |date=2010-07-16 }}</ref> the highest medical research award given in the United States, jointly with [[Robert Gallo]] and [[Luc Montagnier]] in 1986. He has published over 500 papers and 12 books, including two editions of ''AIDS in Africa'' ({{ISBN|0306466996}}), and his latest, ''Saturday Is for Funerals'' ({{ISBN|0674050770}}).  Essex has worked in twelve (12) different nations as a [[veterinarian]] and [[virologist]]: Botswana, China, Colombia, India, Japan, Nigeria, Senegal, Taiwan, Tanzania, Thailand, U.S., Zaire.<ref name="haispotlight" />

His 45 years of working papers, the Myron Essex papers, 1949–1996, are archived in the Countway Library's Center for the History of Medicine through funding by a Hidden Collections grant from the [[Harvard University Library]] (HUL) within the Maximizing Microbiology: Molecular Genetics, Cancer, and Virology, 1936-2000 project.  In addition to the Myron Essex papers (1949–1996), the project has already led to the processing of collections of several other microbiologists, including those of Bernard D. Davis, Arthur B. Pardee, Francesc Duran i Reynals, and Luigi Gorini.  Essex serves on the Library's Archives Committee.<ref>[https://aids.harvard.edu/people/max-essex/ Harvard AIDS Institute Profile Page for Max Essex]</ref>  In 2018 Dr. Essex announced his retirement plans.<ref name="haispotlight" />

He has been the primary mentor to eighty (80) postdocs and to 34 doctoral students.  He has authored 629 research papers, forty (40) of which have been published in ''Science'' or ''Nature''.<ref name="haispotlight" />

==Awards==
* Elected member, Institute of Medicine (IOM) of the National Academy of Sciences (NAS, now NASEM){{citation needed|date=November 2018}}
* Fellow, American Academy of Microbiology{{citation needed|date=November 2018}}
* HIV Lifetime Achievement Award for Scientific Contributions from the Institute of Human Virology (IHV) at the University of Maryland School of Medicine, November 2011<ref>[https://aids.harvard.edu/essex-receives-lifetime-achievement-award-spotlight-fall-2011/ Henry MS.  Essex Receives Lifetime Achievement Award.  December 1, 2011.  HAI Blog]</ref>
* Lifetime Achievement Award, AIDS Society of India, 2014 (in Kolkata).  The plaque reads “For his exemplary contribution towards research in HIV/AIDS and for his outstanding leadership in public health.”{{citation needed|date=November 2018}}

==Awards named for Max Essex==
* Essex Fellowship for Students from Africa, [[Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health]], annually since 2007
